key_insight: The arithmetic holds: a 1-bit mask plus per-row scales is ~1/16 of bf16, so 1,000 full fine-tunes cost ~63 base copies instead of 1,000 (~16x).
killer_doubt: BitDelta already fuses 1-bit deltas into the matmul, and LoRA adapters are 0.1-1% of the base. Multi-tenant full-fine-tune serving is well under 1% of DRAM demand.
decisive_experiment: Nothing new is needed. Reproduce BitDelta serving 100 Llama-3-8B variants on one 8-GPU node and measure resident GB and tokens/s against S-LoRA (<$20k).
prior_art: BitDelta (2024) fused 1-bit deltas; DeltaZip; ComPEFT sparse ternary residuals; S-LoRA/Punica adapter serving. From memory.

key_insight: The software multiplier is real: a byte saved in Redis or Chromium is saved on millions of machines, and a CI harness measuring RSS is cheap and objective.
killer_doubt: Fleets provision DRAM by VM shape and configured buffer pools, not RSS, so a 10% benchmark cut frees ~0% until operators resize. Meta's TMO offload already saves ~20-32% (from memory).
decisive_experiment: Before funding bounties, merge 3 known memory-saving patches in each of 5 packages. At 2 partner operators, track over 6 months whether instance sizing or GB purchased changes (<$100k).
prior_art: Google Patch Rewards; Sovereign Tech Fund; Valkey 8 per-key overhead cuts; Meta TMO and Google zswap far memory. From memory.

key_insight: The sharing is exact, not approximate. Freeze layers 1..k and their K/V projections, and their prefix KV is identical by construction, so N variants store k+N(L-k) layers.
killer_doubt: It helps only prefix KV shared across variants, capped at 2x on that slice when k=L/2. Activated LoRA already reuses base KV for the whole prefix at every layer.
decisive_experiment: Fine-tune Llama-3-8B with LoRA on only the top 8, 16 or 24 of 32 layers for 5 tasks and measure quality loss. Replay a multi-LoRA trace to measure the shared-prefix KV fraction (<$30k).
prior_art: IBM Activated LoRA (2025) base-KV reuse; DroidSpeak (2024) cross-fine-tune KV reuse with selective recompute; SGLang RadixAttention. From memory.

key_insight: The capacity bound favours it: tail IDs with few interactions carry little learned information, so a generator covers them while explicit rows for the hottest ~1% keep memorisation.
killer_doubt: Production tables already ship pruned and int4 (~4-8x). A light DHE decoder costs ~0.7 uJ per lookup, ~50x a 128 B fetch (~15 nJ). Production NE loss is unmeasured.
decisive_experiment: Train DLRM on Criteo-1TB with four tables: full, int4 plus pruning, the CAFE hot/hash hybrid and a DHE hybrid. Report NE against bytes and FLOPs per lookup. Pass: >=5x smaller than int4-pruned at <0.02% NE loss (<$50k).
prior_art: DHE (Kang et al., KDD 2021); TT-Rec (MLSys 2021); ROBE (MLSys 2022); CAFE hot/hashed hybrid (SIGMOD 2024); QR embeddings (KDD 2020). From memory.

key_insight: The right framing: the floor is Kolmogorov complexity. Seeded-PRNG content (random projections, hashed weights, SeedLM codes) defeats line compressors yet is trivial to generate.
killer_doubt: Zero pages and BDI compression already catch cheap generators. An MLP generator needs ~1 MFLOP, ~1 us per line versus 50-100 ns DRAM. In-kernel recomputation needs no new PTE type.
decisive_experiment: Dump memory from 50 production servers and classify 64 B lines as zero/constant, BDI-compressible or neither. Test the residue for PRNG or affine generators. Advance only if >5% is generator-only (<$40k).
prior_art: Linux zero page and KSM; Base-Delta-Immediate (PACT 2012); userfaultfd lazy fill; SeedLM (Apple 2024) PRNG-seed weights. From memory.

key_insight: AI servers size host DRAM to GPU count, not need (DGX H100: 2 TB per 640 GB HBM). Installed base ~1 EB (estimate); sub-5 us RDMA paging suits cold tiers.
killer_doubt: The GPUs are claiming the idle bytes themselves: KV offload tiers (Mooncake, LMCache, Dynamo) and in-memory checkpoints. Above ~70% utilisation, harvestable supply drops below ~0.3 EB.
decisive_experiment: Collect 30 days of host-memory telemetry (RSS, page cache, pinned, KV tier) on 2-3 GPU clusters. Then run an Infiniswap/Fastswap-style lease to CPU tenants and measure p99 slowdown on both sides (<$150k).
prior_art: Infiniswap (NSDI 2017); Fastswap (<5 us, via search snippet); Memtrade harvesting marketplace (via search snippet); Harvest VMs. GPU-host-specific: none found.

key_insight: WebGraph reaches ~2-3 bits/link on web graphs, against 32-64 bits for raw adjacency, so a 10-20x footprint cut is real for web-crawl graphs.
killer_doubt: Social graphs compress only to ~8-12 bits/edge (~3-4x). Software decoders (Ligra+) already run near uncompressed speed, and SpZip built the hardware. Graph analytics is a tiny share of DRAM.
decisive_experiment: Nothing new is needed at first. Benchmark Ligra+ and WebGraph-decoded BFS and PageRank on Twitter and ClueWeb against SpZip's published results. Add hardware only if software decode is >2x slower (<$20k).
prior_art: WebGraph (Boldi-Vigna 2004); Ligra+ (DCC 2015); Log(Graph) (PACT 2018); SpZip hardware decompression (ISCA 2021). From memory.

key_insight: Pointer-heavy structures do carry 5-20x overhead over their information content, and succinct layouts (LOUDS, Elias-Fano) reach near-entropy size.
killer_doubt: Software already gets the memory saving; popcnt/pdep rank/select take ~10 ns. Each hop costs 2-3 dependent ~100 ns misses; a controller engine saves only the ~40 ns on-chip round trip.
decisive_experiment: Profile SDSL-lite rank/select and Elias-Fano traversal on graph, trie and inverted-index workloads. Model in gem5 a controller-side engine that removes the on-chip round trip. Advance only if speedup >2x (<$30k).
prior_art: SDSL-lite; Succinct (NSDI 2015); near-memory FM-index accelerators (GenStore, MEDAL); SpZip (ISCA 2021). From memory.

key_insight: The same mechanism as I-06735 without the hot-row cache. Tensor cores make the decoder MLP cheap in FLOPs per dollar, though not in energy.
killer_doubt: With no stored rows, a ~1e7-parameter generator cannot hold the memorised information of hot IDs from a 1e9-row table. Published DHE results come from small datasets, not production NE.
decisive_experiment: Covered by I-06735's experiment: add a DHE arm with no hot rows on Criteo-1TB and report its NE gap against the hybrid (<$10k extra).
prior_art: Deep Hash Embedding (KDD 2021); TT-Rec (MLSys 2021); ROBE (MLSys 2022). From memory.

key_insight: Identical to I-06735: DHE plus exact rows for the hottest 1% of IDs. The hybrid is the right deployable shape.
killer_doubt: A duplicate of I-06735, and the hybrid is already published: CAFE gives hot IDs exclusive rows and hashes the rest. Its gain over int4-pruned tables is unmeasured at production scale.
decisive_experiment: Covered by I-06735's Criteo-1TB comparison; no separate experiment is warranted.
prior_art: DHE (KDD 2021); CAFE (SIGMOD 2024); mixed-dimension embeddings (Ginart et al. 2019). From memory.

key_insight: A per-ID sign is a cheap collision decorrelator (1 bit/ID, ~125 MB for 1e9 IDs). With multiple hashes, a 100x smaller table keeps most of the tail's information.
killer_doubt: This is feature hashing, hash embeddings and QR embeddings. A per-ID fp16 scale costs 2 B against a 128 B row, capping the gain at 64x, below the claimed 100x.
decisive_experiment: Nothing new is needed. Reproduce QR and hash embeddings on Criteo-1TB at 100x compression, with and without the per-ID sign, and report NE (<$10k).
prior_art: Feature hashing (Weinberger 2009); Hash Embeddings (Svenstrup 2017); QR embeddings (Shi et al. KDD 2020); ROBE (2022). From memory.

key_insight: Pyramid summaries in HBM, with full-resolution spans in flash rather than DRAM, make resident KV grow roughly logarithmically with context. HBM is the costliest bit (~3x DDR5 wafer area).
killer_doubt: Flash bandwidth: Llama-3-70B KV is ~320 KB/token, so a 4k-token recall budget is ~1.3 GB per step. At 10% churn per 30 ms step, one sequence needs ~4.5 GB/s.
decisive_experiment: Log attention mass per 64-token span on 128k-1M-context traces (Llama-3-70B; RULER, LongBench), measuring span churn per step and accuracy with one-step-lagged recall. Replay the recall stream on 4 NVMe drives (<$60k).
prior_art: ArkVale (NeurIPS 2024) page summaries plus recall; InfLLM; Quest; ShadowKV; InfiniGen (OSDI 2024); InstInfer in-SSD attention. From memory.
